canonical_data: Ingested files and artifact nodes under the operator's local data folder, with the vector, document, and index stores chosen per install (Qdrant for vectors; PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, or DB2 for the document and index stores), plus application-held message history.
current_repo_note: The record covers PrivateGPT 1.0, "rebuilt from the ground up as a proper API layer for private AI applications". The 2023 proof of concept that gave the repository its following was a local chat-with-your-documents script, which is a different product and is not this record; the bundled /ui workbench ships with the release and is described by the maintainers as "a demonstrator, not the core product". The vendor's commercial Zylon platform is built on this code and is not reviewed here.
strengths: Mirrors the Claude API surface feature for feature, so agent code, tools, and MCP clients written against one run against local models on the other
Runs against any OpenAI-compatible server rather than a model vendor, with an offline mode setting for air-gapped installs
Local by default: ingested files and artifact nodes stay in the operator's data folder, and the vector, document, and index stores are chosen per install
Built-in tools go past retrieval to web search, web fetch, and code execution, with custom tools and remote MCP servers alongside them
weaknesses: The shipped settings enable no authentication and allow every CORS origin, so an operator who exposes the port exposes the tool surface, code execution included, until they turn auth on
It is an API layer rather than an agent: the loop, the plan, and failure recovery belong to the application built on top, so the framework scores the caller's work as its own capability surface
The maintainers' own comparison marks skills as basic, batch and async as async-only, structured outputs as inference-dependent, and prompt caching and OAuth as unsupported
Repository popularity measures the 2023 script rather than the 1.0 rewrite: the current release line began at v1.0.0 on 2026-06-03, so the star count overstates how long this code has been a product
why_it_matters: The reference answer to the question a private deployment actually asks, which is not which model to run but what to put in front of it: one API surface that keeps a laptop and a datacentre on the same client code, with the data never leaving the operator's hardware.
